name: ERGOTAMINE TARTARATE
uses: Acute attack of migraine unresponsive to analgesics; menopausal hot flushes.
indications: Acute attack of migraine unresponsive to analgesics; menopausal hot flushes.
side_effects: Arterial spasm, intermittent claudication, neck stiffness, numbness or tingling.
adverse_effects: Arterial spasm, intermittent claudication, neck stiffness, numbness or tingling.
dosage: Migraine: 2mg sublingual then 1.2mg every 30mins (max 6mg/day, 10mg/week). Menopausal flushes: 0.6mg PO q12h.
dosage_schedule: Migraine: 2mg sublingual then 1.2mg every 30mins (max 6mg/day, 10mg/week). Menopausal flushes: 0.6mg PO q12h.
precautions: Sepsis, malnutrition, impaired renal/hepatic function. Should be initiated at first sign of vascular headache.
contraindications: PVD, CAD, Raynaud’s disease, pregnancy/lactation, severe HTN. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, macrolides, antifungals).
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors may produce life-threatening peripheral ischemia.

name: RIZATRIPTAN
uses: Acute migraine.
indications: Acute migraine.
side_effects: Decreased alertness, drowsiness, pharyngeal discomfort.
adverse_effects: Decreased alertness, drowsiness, pharyngeal discomfort.
dosage: Oral, adult: 10 mg as soon as possible, follow with 10 mg after 2 hours if required (max 20 mg/day).
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 10 mg as soon as possible, follow with 10 mg after 2 hours if required (max 20 mg/day).
precautions: Hepatic/renal impairment, pregnancy. Drowsiness may affect performance of skilled tasks.
contraindications: Severe hypertension, coronary vasospasm, ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, history of MI/TIA/CVA.
interactions: May enhance toxic effects of serotonin modulators.
pregnancy_category_notes: Present in milk; withhold breast-feeding for 24 hours.

name: SUMATRIPTAN
uses: Acute migraine attacks, cluster headache.
indications: Acute migraine attacks, cluster headache.
side_effects: Injection site reaction, jaw or neck tightness, diaphoresis.
adverse_effects: Injection site reaction, jaw or neck tightness, diaphoresis.
dosage: Oral: 50-100 mg. SC injection: 6 mg (max 12 mg in 24 hours). Cluster headache: 6mg SC; may repeat in > 1hr.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50-100 mg. SC injection: 6 mg (max 12 mg in 24 hours). Cluster headache: 6mg SC; may repeat in > 1hr.
precautions: Should not be given intravenously (may cause vasospasm). Avoid breast feeding for 8-12 hrs after administration.
contraindications: Ischemic cardiac/cerebrovascular/peripheral vascular syndromes, WPW syndrome, uncontrolled HTN, use within 2 weeks of MAO-A inhibitors.

name: FLUNARIZINE
uses: Migraine prophylaxis.
indications: Migraine prophylaxis.
side_effects: Drowsiness, extrapyramidal effects, depression in elderly, weight gain, galactorrhea.
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, extrapyramidal effects, depression in elderly, weight gain, galactorrhea.
dosage: Oral, adult: 10-20 mg once daily; child: 5 mg once daily.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 10-20 mg once daily; child: 5 mg once daily.
precautions: May cause CNS depression. Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms.
contraindications: Depression, acute phase of stroke, extrapyramidal symptoms or Parkinson’s disease.
interactions: Effects of alcohol and sedating drugs can be increased.

name: PREGABALIN
uses: Peripheral and central neuropathic pain, adjunct for focal seizures, generalized anxiety disorder.
indications: Peripheral and central neuropathic pain, adjunct for focal seizures, generalized anxiety disorder.
side_effects: Appetite changes, weight gain, visual field defects, impaired memory, speech disorder.
adverse_effects: Appetite changes, weight gain, visual field defects, impaired memory, speech disorder.
dosage: Neuropathic pain: initially 150 mg daily, increase to 600 mg. Focal seizures: initially 25 mg twice daily. GAD: initially 150 mg daily.
dosage_schedule: Neuropathic pain: initially 150 mg daily, increase to 600 mg. Focal seizures: initially 25 mg twice daily. GAD: initially 150 mg daily.
precautions: Conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy, severe CHF, renal impairment. Avoid abrupt withdrawal (taper over 1 week).
interactions: Increased CNS depression if taken with alcohol.

name: BUPRENORPHINE
uses: Perioperative analgesia; moderate to severe pain; withdrawing opioid addicts; chronic non-malignant pain.
indications: Perioperative analgesia; moderate to severe pain; withdrawing opioid addicts; chronic non-malignant pain.
side_effects: See under Morphine; less abuse potential than Morphine.
adverse_effects: See under Morphine; less abuse potential than Morphine.
dosage: IM/Slow IV: 300-600 µg every 6-8hrs. Sublingual tablet: 200-400 µg every 8hrs.
dosage_schedule: IM/Slow IV: 300-600 µg every 6-8hrs. Sublingual tablet: 200-400 µg every 8hrs.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Keep naloxone on hand.
contraindications: Drug overdose can result in coma/death.

name: METHADONE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Severe pain, adjunct in treatment of opioid dependence, cough in terminal disease.
indications: Severe pain, adjunct in treatment of opioid dependence, cough in terminal disease.
side_effects: See under Morphine.
adverse_effects: See under Morphine.
dosage: Opioid dependence: initially 10-40mg daily, increase by max 10mg daily to usual range 60-120 mg.
dosage_schedule: Opioid dependence: initially 10-40mg daily, increase by max 10mg daily to usual range 60-120 mg.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Not recommended to children.
interactions: Rifampicin and Phenytoin accelerate metabolism (can precipitate withdrawal).

name: MORPHINE SULPHATE
uses: Severe pain, MI, acute pulmonary edema, adjunct during major surgery and post-operative analgesia.
indications: Severe pain, MI, acute pulmonary edema, adjunct during major surgery and post-operative analgesia.
side_effects: Classic triad: pinpoint pupil, respiratory depression, coma. Mental clouding, urinary retention, apnoea in newborn.
adverse_effects: Classic triad: pinpoint pupil, respiratory depression, coma. Mental clouding, urinary retention, apnoea in newborn.
dosage: Acute pain (SC/IM): 10mg every 4 hours. MI (IV): 2mg/min, 10mg followed by further 5-10mg.
dosage_schedule: Acute pain (SC/IM): 10mg every 4 hours. MI (IV): 2mg/min, 10mg followed by further 5-10mg.
precautions: Elderly/debilitated, dependence, convulsive disorders. Obtain baseline respiratory rate and pupil size. Bedside rails advisable.
contraindications: Respiratory insufficiency, bronchial asthma, undiagnosed acute abdominal pain, head injury.

name: PETHIDINE HYDROCHLORIDE (MEPERIDINE)
uses: Moderate to severe pain and for obstetric analgesia.
indications: Moderate to severe pain and for obstetric analgesia.
side_effects: Similar to morphine; more severe nausea and hypotension. Equianalgesic doses produce similar respiratory depression.
adverse_effects: Similar to morphine; more severe nausea and hypotension. Equianalgesic doses produce similar respiratory depression.
dosage: PO: 50-150mg every 4 hours. IM/SC: 25-100mg. Obstetrical analgesia: 50-100mg (max 400mg in 24 hours).
dosage_schedule: PO: 50-150mg every 4 hours. IM/SC: 25-100mg. Obstetrical analgesia: 50-100mg (max 400mg in 24 hours).
precautions: May cause life-threatening respiratory depression. Potential for addiction and abuse.
interactions: With MAO-I may cause serious (possibly fatal) reaction.

name: TRAMADOL HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Moderate pain, adjunct in chronic pain.
indications: Moderate pain, adjunct in chronic pain.
side_effects: Seizures, somnolence, nausea.
adverse_effects: Seizures, somnolence, nausea.
dosage: Oral: 50-100mg q4h (total >400mg not usually required). IM/IV/Infusion: 50-100mg every 4-6hrs.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50-100mg q4h (total >400mg not usually required). IM/IV/Infusion: 50-100mg every 4-6hrs.
precautions: Do not confuse with Toradol (Ketorolac). Monitor for seizure.
interactions: CNS depressants (increased risk); B-Lactam antibiotics (increased seizure risk).

name: NALOXONE
uses: Opioid overdose (coma and respiratory depression), neonatal asphyxia, postoperative opioid reversal.
indications: Opioid overdose (coma and respiratory depression), neonatal asphyxia, postoperative opioid reversal.
side_effects: Sweating, withdrawal symptoms in opioid abusers.
adverse_effects: Sweating, withdrawal symptoms in opioid abusers.
dosage: Adult IV: 0.4-2mg repeated at 2-3 min intervals (max 10mg). Child: 10μg/kg.
dosage_schedule: Adult IV: 0.4-2mg repeated at 2-3 min intervals (max 10mg). Child: 10μg/kg.
precautions: Physical dependence on opioids (may precipitate acute withdrawal).
interactions: Antagonizes the effects of opioid analgesics.

name: NALTREXONE
uses: Opioid dependence, alcohol dependence, herpetic neuralgia, Crohn’s disease in children.
indications: Opioid dependence, alcohol dependence, herpetic neuralgia, Crohn’s disease in children.
side_effects: Injection site reaction, decreased appetite, arthralgia.
adverse_effects: Injection site reaction, decreased appetite, arthralgia.
dosage: Chronic opioid dependence: PO 25mg day 1, then 50mg once daily. IM: 380mg every 4 weeks.
dosage_schedule: Chronic opioid dependence: PO 25mg day 1, then 50mg once daily. IM: 380mg every 4 weeks.
precautions: Risk of hepatotoxicity with increasing doses. Discontinue if signs of acute hepatitis develop.
contraindications: Currently dependent on opioids; acute hepatitis or liver failure.

name: PENTAZOCINE
uses: Moderate to severe pain, preoperative/pre-anesthetic supplement.
indications: Moderate to severe pain, preoperative/pre-anesthetic supplement.
side_effects: Pulmonary artery hypertension, tolerance, dependence.
adverse_effects: Pulmonary artery hypertension, tolerance, dependence.
dosage: Oral: 50mg q3-4h. Severe pain: 45-60mg IM/IV q3-4h.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50mg q3-4h. Severe pain: 45-60mg IM/IV q3-4h.
precautions: Use cautiously in acute asthma, bradycardia. May produce acute withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent users.
contraindications: Toxin-mediated diarrhea, Pseudomonas enterocolitis, respiratory depression, MI.

name: MIRTAZAPINE
uses: Major depression, PTSD (off label), insomnia (off label).
indications: Major depression, PTSD (off label), insomnia (off label).
side_effects: Somnolence, xerostomia, weight gain, reversible agranulocytosis.
adverse_effects: Somnolence, xerostomia, weight gain, reversible agranulocytosis.
dosage: Depression (Adult): 15 mg PO HS; increase to max 60 mg HS. Geriatric: 7.5 mg PO HS.
dosage_schedule: Depression (Adult): 15 mg PO HS; increase to max 60 mg HS. Geriatric: 7.5 mg PO HS.
precautions: Start slowly in hepatic/renal dysfunction. Discontinue if neutropenia/agranulocytosis occur.
interactions: Do not use within 14 days of MAOI.

name: FLUOXETINE
uses: Major depression, OCD, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder.
indications: Major depression, OCD, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder.
side_effects: Insomnia, sexual dysfunction, taste disturbances, serotonin syndrome.
adverse_effects: Insomnia, sexual dysfunction, taste disturbances, serotonin syndrome.
dosage: Adult Depression/OCD: Initial 20 mg PO daily; max 80 mg/day. Bulimia: 60 mg once daily.
dosage_schedule: Adult Depression/OCD: Initial 20 mg PO daily; max 80 mg/day. Bulimia: 60 mg once daily.
precautions: Monitor closely for suicidal tendencies. Discontinue if symptomatic hyponatremia occurs.
interactions: Do not use with MAO inhibitors (within 14 days). Do not use with linezolid or pimozide.

name: LITHIUM
uses: Prophylaxis and treatment of mania, prophylaxis of bipolar disorder, hyperthyroidism.
indications: Prophylaxis and treatment of mania, prophylaxis of bipolar disorder, hyperthyroidism.
side_effects: Fine tremor, polydipsia, weight gain, acne, oedema.
adverse_effects: Fine tremor, polydipsia, weight gain, acne, oedema.
dosage: Up to 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses; adjusted by plasma concentration.
dosage_schedule: Up to 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses; adjusted by plasma concentration.
precautions: Regularly monitor serum lithium levels and thyroid/renal function. Lithium crosses placenta.
contraindications: Hypothyroidism, sick sinus syndrome, heart blocks, renal diseases.
interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac) and ACE inhibitors increase serum concentrations by reducing excretion.
pregnancy_category_notes: Use during pregnancy only in life-threatening situations.

name: ALPRAZOLAM
uses: Anxiety disorders, agoraphobia, panic disorders, depression.
indications: Anxiety disorders, agoraphobia, panic disorders, depression.
side_effects: Confusion, physical dependence, changes in libido.
adverse_effects: Confusion, physical dependence, changes in libido.
dosage: 0.25 to 0.5 mg TID; max total daily 3 mg. Elderly: 0.25 mg BID/TID.
dosage_schedule: 0.25 to 0.5 mg TID; max total daily 3 mg. Elderly: 0.25 mg BID/TID.
precautions: Monitor respiratory function. Watch for signs of tolerance and dependence.
contraindications: Respiratory depression, severe hepatic impairment, angle closure glaucoma.
interactions: Increases sedative effect of opioid analgesics.

name: ZOLPIDEM
uses: Insomnia.
indications: Insomnia.
side_effects: Nightmares, asthenia, memory disturbances, ataxia.
adverse_effects: Nightmares, asthenia, memory disturbances, ataxia.
dosage: 10 mg at bedtime; elderly 5 mg.
dosage_schedule: 10 mg at bedtime; elderly 5 mg.
precautions: Use with caution in depression.
contraindications: Children, severe hepatic/pulmonary insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, obstructive sleep apnea.

name: HALOTHANE
uses: Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia
indications: Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia
side_effects: Nausea and vomiting, acidosis, dehydration and fever in children (may predispose to convulsions under ether anaesthesia). May cause excessive bleeding during caesarean section and post-partum haemorrhage.
adverse_effects: Nausea and vomiting, acidosis, dehydration and fever in children (may predispose to convulsions under ether anaesthesia). May cause excessive bleeding during caesarean section and post-partum haemorrhage.
dosage: Induction: Done using a special calibrated vaporizer, increased gradually to 2-4% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen; child: 1.5-2%. Maintenance: 0.5-2%.
dosage_schedule: Induction: Done using a special calibrated vaporizer, increased gradually to 2-4% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen; child: 1.5-2%. Maintenance: 0.5-2%.
precautions: Careful anaesthetic history should be taken to determine previous exposure and previous reaction to halothane.
contraindications: History of unexplained jaundice or pyrexia in a patient following exposure to halothane. Avoid repeated exposure to halothane in less than three months.
interactions: With adrenaline, heart is sensitized to the actions of catecholamines.

name: ISOFLURANE
uses: Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia (usually not preferred for induction due to ether-like odor)
indications: Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia (usually not preferred for induction due to ether-like odor)
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, shivering, dose-dependent hypotension, arrhythmia, respiratory depression (rare), risk of perioperative hyperkalemia and malignant hypertension (especially in Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy).
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, shivering, dose-dependent hypotension, arrhythmia, respiratory depression (rare), risk of perioperative hyperkalemia and malignant hypertension (especially in Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy).
dosage: Using a special calibrated vaporizer. Induction: Increased gradually from 0.5% to 3% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen. Maintenance: 1-2.5% in nitrous oxide-oxygen; an additional 0.5-1% may be required when given with oxygen alone.
dosage_schedule: Using a special calibrated vaporizer. Induction: Increased gradually from 0.5% to 3% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen. Maintenance: 1-2.5% in nitrous oxide-oxygen; an additional 0.5-1% may be required when given with oxygen alone.
precautions: Use cautiously in lactation. Safety and efficacy not established in pediatric patients.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to isoflurane and halogenated agents, genetic susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia. Coronary artery disease; should not be used as a sole agent of induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction.
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine has been associated with hyperkalemia and potentiation of muscle relaxant action.

name: NITROUS OXIDE
uses: Used as a carrier gas for more powerful general anesthetic drugs like desflurane and sevoflurane
indications: Used as a carrier gas for more powerful general anesthetic drugs like desflurane and sevoflurane
side_effects: Megaloblastic anemia due to Vit. B12 and folate deficiency; teratogenic (avoid in 1st and 2nd trimester).
adverse_effects: Megaloblastic anemia due to Vit. B12 and folate deficiency; teratogenic (avoid in 1st and 2nd trimester).
dosage: Mixture with 50% O2 during labor.
dosage_schedule: Mixture with 50% O2 during labor.
precautions: Should be used cautiously in 1st and 2nd trimester of pregnancy and in patient with decreased level of consciousness or in violently disturbed psychiatric patient.
contraindications: Pneumothorax, pneumoperitoneum, middle ear or sinus disease, bowel obstruction.
interactions: When given with other strong anesthetic drugs like desflurane and isoflurane, effect of both drugs increases.

name: OXYGEN
uses: Along with inhalational anesthesia, cluster headache, hyperbaric oxygen (decompression sickness, air/gas embolism, gas gangrene, necrotising fasciitis, radiation therapy), respiratory failure.
indications: Along with inhalational anesthesia, cluster headache, hyperbaric oxygen (decompression sickness, air/gas embolism, gas gangrene, necrotising fasciitis, radiation therapy), respiratory failure.
side_effects: Concentrations >80% have toxic lung effects (pulmonary congestion, exudation, atelectasis). Retinopathy of prematurity. Hyperbaric therapy may cause barotrauma or CNS/pulmonary toxicity.
adverse_effects: Concentrations >80% have toxic lung effects (pulmonary congestion, exudation, atelectasis). Retinopathy of prematurity. Hyperbaric therapy may cause barotrauma or CNS/pulmonary toxicity.
dosage: During anesthesia/general: Nasal prongs or face mask (up to 60%); Tight-fitting masks or ETT (up to 100%). Respiratory failure: Face masks at 5 L/min. Cluster headache: Inhalation of 100% oxygen. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy: Intermittent inhalation of 100% oxygen under pressure >1 atmosphere in a specialized chamber.
dosage_schedule: During anesthesia/general: Nasal prongs or face mask (up to 60%); Tight-fitting masks or ETT (up to 100%). Respiratory failure: Face masks at 5 L/min. Cluster headache: Inhalation of 100% oxygen. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy: Intermittent inhalation of 100% oxygen under pressure >1 atmosphere in a specialized chamber.
precautions: Valves and taps should not be lubricated with oil or grease. Any fire or spark is highly dangerous in the presence of increased oxygen concentrations.
contraindications: Avoid high concentrations in patients whose respiration is dependent upon hypoxic drive.

name: SEVOFLURANE
uses: Anesthesia
indications: Anesthesia
side_effects: Malignant hyperthermia, dose-dependent hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, apnea, increased BUN/ALT, nephrotoxicity, glycosuria, proteinuria.
adverse_effects: Malignant hyperthermia, dose-dependent hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, apnea, increased BUN/ALT, nephrotoxicity, glycosuria, proteinuria.
dosage: Surgical anaesthesia: Inhalation. 0.5 months full term neonate: 3.3% in O2; 1-6 months: 3% in O2; 6 mo-3 years: 2.8% in O2; 25-40 years: 2.1% in O2; 60-80 years: 1.4% in O2 (detailed age-based ranges in formulary).
dosage_schedule: Surgical anaesthesia: Inhalation. 0.5 months full term neonate: 3.3% in O2; 1-6 months: 3% in O2; 6 mo-3 years: 2.8% in O2; 25-40 years: 2.1% in O2; 60-80 years: 1.4% in O2 (detailed age-based ranges in formulary).
precautions: Caution in patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, renal impairment, or QTc prolongation.
contraindications: Should not be used as a sole agent for induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction. Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia, hypersensitivity, lack of ventilatory support.
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine associated with hyperkalemia.

name: KETAMINE
uses: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia for minor surgical or diagnostic procedures; Analgesia for painful procedures of short duration for patients at risk of hypotension and bronchospasm.
indications: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia for minor surgical or diagnostic procedures; Analgesia for painful procedures of short duration for patients at risk of hypotension and bronchospasm.
side_effects: Emergence reactions (dreams, hallucinations, delirium), hypertension, increased cardiac output, increased ICP, tachycardia, tonic clonic movements, increased salivation, dependence.
adverse_effects: Emergence reactions (dreams, hallucinations, delirium), hypertension, increased cardiac output, increased ICP, tachycardia, tonic clonic movements, increased salivation, dependence.
dosage: IM injection (short procedures): Initially 6.5-13 mg/kg. IV injection (diagnostic): Initially 4 mg/kg over at least 60 seconds. IV infusion (short procedures): Initially 1-4.5 mg/kg. Induction: 0.5-2 mg/kg. Maintenance: 10-45 mcg/kg/minute.
dosage_schedule: IM injection (short procedures): Initially 6.5-13 mg/kg. IV injection (diagnostic): Initially 4 mg/kg over at least 60 seconds. IV infusion (short procedures): Initially 1-4.5 mg/kg. Induction: 0.5-2 mg/kg. Maintenance: 10-45 mcg/kg/minute.
precautions: Use cautiously in CNS abnormalities, hydrocephalus, increased IOP, CAD, catecholamine depletion. To be administered only by experienced personnel with immediate availability of respiratory/cardiovascular support.
contraindications: Patients with epilepsy, hypertension, and in patients with increased ICP.
interactions: With diazepam, may cause ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation.

name: MIDAZOLAM
uses: Status epilepticus, febrile convulsions, conscious sedation for procedures, sedative in combined anaesthesia, premedication, sedation in intensive care, confusion/restlessness in palliative care; Status tonic-clonic seizures in patients undergoing dental treatment
indications: Status epilepticus, febrile convulsions, conscious sedation for procedures, sedative in combined anaesthesia, premedication, sedation in intensive care, confusion/restlessness in palliative care; Status tonic-clonic seizures in patients undergoing dental treatment
side_effects: Decreased respiratory rate, apnea, drowsiness, seizure-like activity, nausea/vomiting, sedation, delirium, euphoria; Low blood pressure, respiratory depression
adverse_effects: Decreased respiratory rate, apnea, drowsiness, seizure-like activity, nausea/vomiting, sedation, delirium, euphoria; Low blood pressure, respiratory depression
dosage: Status epilepticus (buccal): Child 1–11 months: 2.5 mg; 1–4 years: 5 mg; 5–9 years: 7.5 mg; Adult: 10 mg; Conscious sedation (slow IV): Adult: Initially 2–2.5 mg (max 7.5 mg/course); Elderly: Initially 0.5–1 mg (max 3.5 mg/course); Premedication (IM): Adult: 70–100 mcg/kg; Induction (slow IV): Adult: 150–200 mcg/kg daily; Adults: 10 mg; Pediatric: 1-5 years: 5 mg; 5-10 years: 7.5 mg; >10 years: 10 mg
dosage_schedule: Status epilepticus (buccal): Child 1–11 months: 2.5 mg; 1–4 years: 5 mg; 5–9 years: 7.5 mg; Adult: 10 mg; Conscious sedation (slow IV): Adult: Initially 2–2.5 mg (max 7.5 mg/course); Elderly: Initially 0.5–1 mg (max 3.5 mg/course); Premedication (IM): Adult: 70–100 mcg/kg; Induction (slow IV): Adult: 150–200 mcg/kg daily; Adults: 10 mg; Pediatric: 1-5 years: 5 mg; 5-10 years: 7.5 mg; >10 years: 10 mg
precautions: Concentration in children under 15 kg not to exceed 1 mg/mL; Monitor neonates under 6 months for airways obstruction; Caution in hepatic/renal impairment; To be avoided in breastfeeding women; Keep patient supine; Rapid IV injection in neonates can result in low blood pressure and seizures
contraindications: CNS depression, compromised airway, severe respiratory depression; Neonates (rapid IV injection)

name: PROPOFOL
uses: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, sedation for surgical and diagnostic procedures.
indications: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, sedation for surgical and diagnostic procedures.
side_effects: Bradycardia, hypotension, apnea, involuntary movements, injection site burning/stinging, respiratory acidosis during weaning, hypertriglyceridemia.
adverse_effects: Bradycardia, hypotension, apnea, involuntary movements, injection site burning/stinging, respiratory acidosis during weaning, hypertriglyceridemia.
dosage: Induction (IV injection): 1.5-2.5 mg/kg (1-1.5 mg/kg in those >55 years); child 3-16 yrs: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg. Maintenance: IV injection 25-50 mg repeat OR IV infusion 4-12 mg/kg/hour. Sedation: IV injection 0.5-1 mg/kg; IV infusion 1.5-4.5 mg/kg/hour.
dosage_schedule: Induction (IV injection): 1.5-2.5 mg/kg (1-1.5 mg/kg in those >55 years); child 3-16 yrs: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg. Maintenance: IV injection 25-50 mg repeat OR IV infusion 4-12 mg/kg/hour. Sedation: IV injection 0.5-1 mg/kg; IV infusion 1.5-4.5 mg/kg/hour.
precautions: Proper aseptic technique imperative. Risk of fatal propofol infusion syndrome in ICU patients. Closely monitor patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, or renal impairment.
contraindications: Lack of ventilator support, severe cardiac dysfunction, egg/soybean/soy allergy. Sedation of ventilated children and adolescents <17 years. Use in labor and delivery (causes neonatal depression).
interactions: Additive CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol, antihistamines, opioid analgesics, and sedative/hypnotics.

name: THIOPENTAL SODIUM
uses: Induction of anesthesia, rapid control of convulsions like status epilepticus
indications: Induction of anesthesia, rapid control of convulsions like status epilepticus
side_effects: Respiratory and myocardial depression, cardiac arrhythmias, bronchospasm and laryngospasm with cough, rash, prolonged somnolence.
adverse_effects: Respiratory and myocardial depression, cardiac arrhythmias, bronchospasm and laryngospasm with cough, rash, prolonged somnolence.
dosage: Induction of anesthesia: Adult: 100-150 mg (4-6 ml of 2.5% solution); repeat after 30-60 sec depending on response. Child dose: 2-7 mg/kg.
dosage_schedule: Induction of anesthesia: Adult: 100-150 mg (4-6 ml of 2.5% solution); repeat after 30-60 sec depending on response. Child dose: 2-7 mg/kg.
precautions: Anesthesia is deeper whenever protein binding is less (e.g., in liver disease). Slight extravasation risk (severe pain, necrosis). Never give into the arteries.
contraindications: Porphyria, hypersensitivity, breast feeding, hypotension, status asthmaticus, severe cardiovascular diseases, hepatic or renal dysfunction.
interactions: Chemically reacts with succinylcholine; never give in same syringe.

name: BUPIVACAINE
uses: Local infiltration, peripheral nerve block, epidural block, sympathetic block; Local anaesthesia
indications: Local infiltration, peripheral nerve block, epidural block, sympathetic block; Local anaesthesia
side_effects: Headache, bradycardia, hypotension, cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, anxiety, restlessness, tremor, dizziness, respiratory arrest
adverse_effects: Headache, bradycardia, hypotension, cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, anxiety, restlessness, tremor, dizziness, respiratory arrest
dosage: Adjusted per site; Local infiltration: 0.25% (up to 60 ml); Peripheral nerve block: 0.25% (max 60 ml) or 0.5% (max 30 ml); Epidural: 0.5% (max 20-30 ml); Labour (lumbar): 0.25-0.5% (max 12 ml); 0.5% infiltrated
dosage_schedule: Adjusted per site; Local infiltration: 0.25% (up to 60 ml); Peripheral nerve block: 0.25% (max 60 ml) or 0.5% (max 30 ml); Epidural: 0.5% (max 20-30 ml); Labour (lumbar): 0.25-0.5% (max 12 ml); 0.5% infiltrated
precautions: Caution in severely debilitated patients, liver disease, renal impairment, pregnancy, impaired cardiac condition, and myasthenia gravis; Hepatic impairment
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; Do not use for IV anesthesia (QT interval prolongation risk); Do not use for obstetric paracervical block; Hypersensitivity, history of malignant hyperthermia

name: LIDOCAINE (LIGNOCAINE)
uses: Arrhythmia, Local anaesthesia
indications: Arrhythmia, Local anaesthesia
side_effects: See Bupivacaine.
adverse_effects: See Bupivacaine.
dosage: Infiltration (by injection): Maximum dose 200 mg (or 500 mg with adrenaline; maximum adrenaline dose 500 µg). Nerve blocks: 1% to maximum of 40 ml (with adrenaline 1 in 200,000). Surface anaesthesia: Mouth/throat max 200 mg; Urethra 2% gel max 400 mg.
dosage_schedule: Infiltration (by injection): Maximum dose 200 mg (or 500 mg with adrenaline; maximum adrenaline dose 500 µg). Nerve blocks: 1% to maximum of 40 ml (with adrenaline 1 in 200,000). Surface anaesthesia: Mouth/throat max 200 mg; Urethra 2% gel max 400 mg.
precautions: Store at 8-15º C. Discard any gel not used in a single application.

name: PRILOCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE
uses: Infiltration for dentistry, nerve block
indications: Infiltration for dentistry, nerve block
side_effects: See Lidocaine.

dosage: T. solium (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g single dose after breakfast + purgative 2 hours later; (Child 2-6): 1 g; (<2): 500 mg. H. nana (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g day 1, then 1 g daily for 6 days.
dosage_schedule: T. solium (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g single dose after breakfast + purgative 2 hours later; (Child 2-6): 1 g; (<2): 500 mg. H. nana (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g day 1, then 1 g daily for 6 days.
precautions: Inactive against cysticercosis cellulose; danger of cysticercosis in T. solium. Avoid alcohol during treatment.
interactions: Alcohol enhances its absorption and adverse effects.

name: PENTAMIDINE
uses: Visceral leishmaniasis, Pneumocystis pneumonia.
indications: Visceral leishmaniasis, Pneumocystis pneumonia.
side_effects: Acute renal failure, hyperkalaemia, megaloblastic anaemia, acute pancreatitis, pain at site.
adverse_effects: Acute renal failure, hyperkalaemia, megaloblastic anaemia, acute pancreatitis, pain at site.
dosage: Leishmaniasis: deep IM 3-4 mg/kg on alternate days (max 10 injections). Pneumonia: IV infusion 4 mg/kg daily for 14 days.
dosage_schedule: Leishmaniasis: deep IM 3-4 mg/kg on alternate days (max 10 injections). Pneumonia: IV infusion 4 mg/kg daily for 14 days.
precautions: Blood dyscrasias, renal/hepatic disease, diabetes, hypocalcemia. Monitor blood counts.
interactions: Increases nephrotoxicity of vancomycin/cisplatin. QT prolongation with class III antiarrhythmics/chloroquine. Myelosuppression with radiation.

name: PIPERAZINE
uses: Ascariasis, enterobiasis.
indications: Ascariasis, enterobiasis.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, urticaria.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, urticaria.
dosage: Ascariasis: max 3.5 g/day; Child 75 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days. Enterobiasis: max 2.5 g/day; Child 65 mg/kg for 7 days.
dosage_schedule: Ascariasis: max 3.5 g/day; Child 75 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days. Enterobiasis: max 2.5 g/day; Child 65 mg/kg for 7 days.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding (use only if no alternative). Treat all household members concurrently for pinworms. Wash bedding/nightclothes.
interactions: Enhances phenothiazines; risk of seizures. Antagonistic to Pyrantel Pamoate.

name: PRAZIQUANTEL
uses: Taeniasis (T. solium/saginata), hymenolepiasis, diphyllobothriasis, Schistosoma haematobium/japonicum.
indications: Taeniasis (T. solium/saginata), hymenolepiasis, diphyllobothriasis, Schistosoma haematobium/japonicum.
side_effects: Rectal bleeding, urticaria, dizziness.
adverse_effects: Rectal bleeding, urticaria, dizziness.
dosage: T. solium: 10-20 mg/kg single dose. H. nana: 25 mg/kg single dose. S. haematobium: oral 20 mg/kg, then 20 mg/kg after 4-6 hours. S. japonicum: 20 mg/kg TID for 1 day.
dosage_schedule: T. solium: 10-20 mg/kg single dose. H. nana: 25 mg/kg single dose. S. haematobium: oral 20 mg/kg, then 20 mg/kg after 4-6 hours. S. japonicum: 20 mg/kg TID for 1 day.
precautions: Discontinue if cerebral cysticercosis present. Do not drive for 24 hours after treatment.
interactions: Reduced by chloroquine/dexamethasone. Increased by grapefruit/cimetidine.

name: PYRANTEL PAMOATE
uses: Ascariasis, hookworm, pinworm.
indications: Ascariasis, hookworm, pinworm.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, mild GI disturbance.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, mild GI disturbance.
dosage: Adult/Child (>2 yrs): single 10 mg/kg (max 1 g). Pinworms: repeat after 2 weeks. Treat entire household.
dosage_schedule: Adult/Child (>2 yrs): single 10 mg/kg (max 1 g). Pinworms: repeat after 2 weeks. Treat entire household.
precautions: Hepatic impairment, lactation. Wear tight underwear both day and night while taking.

name: SODIUM STIBOGLUCONATE
uses: Leishmaniasis.
indications: Leishmaniasis.
side_effects: Skin rashes, vomiting, abdominal pain, severe cough.
adverse_effects: Skin rashes, vomiting, abdominal pain, severe cough.
dosage: 20 mg/kg daily (max 850 mg) for at least 20 days (IM/IV). Skin lesions: treat for 10 days.
dosage_schedule: 20 mg/kg daily (max 850 mg) for at least 20 days (IM/IV). Skin lesions: treat for 10 days.
precautions: Withdraw if conduction disturbances occur. Monitor ECG. Rapid IV injection can result in cardiovascular collapse.

name: CLOFAZIMINE
uses: Multibacillary leprosy (with rifampicin/dapsone), Type II lepra reaction.
indications: Multibacillary leprosy (with rifampicin/dapsone), Type II lepra reaction.
side_effects: Red discoloration of skin, feces, urine, and infant skin; dry eyes, dry skin, phototoxicity.
adverse_effects: Red discoloration of skin, feces, urine, and infant skin; dry eyes, dry skin, phototoxicity.
dosage: Adult (Multibacillary): supervised 300 mg once a month + self-administered 50 mg daily for 1 year.
dosage_schedule: Adult (Multibacillary): supervised 300 mg once a month + self-administered 50 mg daily for 1 year.
precautions: Avoid if persistent abdominal pain/diarrhea. May discolor soft contact lenses. Risk of ventricular arrhythmias with bedaquiline.

name: DAPSONE
uses: Leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis, Pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis, rhinosporidiosis recurrence.
indications: Leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis, Pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis, rhinosporidiosis recurrence.
side_effects: Hemolytic anaemia (G6PD deficiency), anorexia, nausea, vomiting.
adverse_effects: Hemolytic anaemia (G6PD deficiency), anorexia, nausea, vomiting.
dosage: Multibacillary: 100 mg daily for 1 year. Paucibacillary: 100 mg daily for 6 months. Child (<35 kg): 50 mg or 1-2 mg/kg. Pneumocystis: 100 mg daily.
dosage_schedule: Multibacillary: 100 mg daily for 1 year. Paucibacillary: 100 mg daily for 6 months. Child (<35 kg): 50 mg or 1-2 mg/kg. Pneumocystis: 100 mg daily.
precautions: N/A
contraindications: Cardiac disease, G6PD deficiency, pulmonary disease.
interactions: Pregnancy- Neonatal methemoglobinemia reported in 3rd trimester.

name: ARTEMETHER with LUMEFANTRINE
uses: Acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, chloroquine-resistant non-falciparum malaria.
indications: Acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, chloroquine-resistant non-falciparum malaria.
side_effects: Palpitation, anorexia, abdominal pain, rash.
adverse_effects: Palpitation, anorexia, abdominal pain, rash.
dosage: Adult/Child (>12 yrs): 4 tabs then 5 doses of 4 tabs at 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hrs (Total 24 tabs) with food. Child (5-14 kg): 1 tab initially then 5 further doses. (Detailed weight brackets in formulary).
dosage_schedule: Adult/Child (>12 yrs): 4 tabs then 5 doses of 4 tabs at 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hrs (Total 24 tabs) with food. Child (5-14 kg): 1 tab initially then 5 further doses. (Detailed weight brackets in formulary).
precautions: If trouble swallowing, tablet may be crushed. Dizziness may affect tasks.

name: ARTESUNATE
uses: P. falciparum malaria, especially multidrug resistance.
indications: P. falciparum malaria, especially multidrug resistance.
side_effects: Drug induced fever, neutropenia, cardiotoxicity (high dose), hemolysis (2 wks post-treatment).
adverse_effects: Drug induced fever, neutropenia, cardiotoxicity (high dose), hemolysis (2 wks post-treatment).
dosage: IV/IM: Loading 2 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg at 4 and 24 hours. Thereafter 1 mg/kg daily until patient tolerates oral (max 7 days).
dosage_schedule: IV/IM: Loading 2 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg at 4 and 24 hours. Thereafter 1 mg/kg daily until patient tolerates oral (max 7 days).
precautions: Must be used immediately after reconstitution; discard if cloudy. Protect from light.

name: CHLOROQUINE
uses: Malaria chemoprophylaxis/treatment, RA, lupus erythematosus.
indications: Malaria chemoprophylaxis/treatment, RA, lupus erythematosus.
side_effects: Epigastric discomfort, pruritus, reversible visual disturbance.
adverse_effects: Epigastric discomfort, pruritus, reversible visual disturbance.
dosage: Prophylaxis: 300 mg base once weekly (start 1 wk before, end 4 wks after). Presumptive Treatment: 600 mg base + 45 mg primaquine. Radical Cure (Relapsing): 600 mg base, then 300 mg at 6, 24, 48 hrs + 15 mg primaquine (15 days). RA/Lupus: 150 mg daily.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: 300 mg base once weekly (start 1 wk before, end 4 wks after). Presumptive Treatment: 600 mg base + 45 mg primaquine. Radical Cure (Relapsing): 600 mg base, then 300 mg at 6, 24, 48 hrs + 15 mg primaquine (15 days). RA/Lupus: 150 mg daily.
precautions: Baseline and periodic ophthalmic test (>150 mg/day).
contraindications: Retinal field changes, auditory damage, torsade de pointes, G6PD deficiency, seizures.
interactions: Cimetidine reduces clearance. Increases QT with antiarrhythmics. Increases 2D6 inhibitors/CYP3A inhibitors. Chloroquine decreases rabies vaccine effects.

name: MEFLOQUINE
uses: Treatment and prophylaxis of Malaria (P. falciparum/P. vivax).
indications: Treatment and prophylaxis of Malaria (P. falciparum/P. vivax).
side_effects: Tinnitus, bradycardia, extrasystoles, dizziness, vertigo.
adverse_effects: Tinnitus, bradycardia, extrasystoles, dizziness, vertigo.
dosage: Prophylaxis: 250 mg weekly (start 2.5 wks before, end 4 wks after). Long term (>3 mo): on individual assessment. Child (<15 kg): not recommended.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: 250 mg weekly (start 2.5 wks before, end 4 wks after). Long term (>3 mo): on individual assessment. Child (<15 kg): not recommended.
precautions: Cardiac conduction disorder, brain injury. Disturbed balance may persist for months after stopping.
contraindications: History of convulsion, psychiatric disorder, infants <3 months, pregnancy.
interactions: Avoid beta-blockers/calcium channel blockers (risk of bradycardia).

name: PRIMAQUINE
uses: Adjunct in P. vivax and P. ovale malaria.
indications: Adjunct in P. vivax and P. ovale malaria.
side_effects: Abdominal cramps, vomiting, leucocytosis, haemolytic anaemia.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, vomiting, leucocytosis, haemolytic anaemia.
dosage: Presumptive: 45 mg single dose. Radical cure: 15 mg daily for 5 days; child 250 mcg/kg daily.
dosage_schedule: Presumptive: 45 mg single dose. Radical cure: 15 mg daily for 5 days; child 250 mcg/kg daily.
precautions: G6PD deficiency risk. Always give in conjunction with chloroquine.
contraindications: Children <1 yr, lupus, RA, methemoglobin reductase deficiency, bone marrow suppression.
interactions: Grapefruit decreases effect. Don't use with other drugs liable to induce hemolysis.

name: QUININE
uses: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
indications: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
side_effects: Cinchonism (tinnitus, temporary blindness, blurred vision, hot skin), hypoglycemia, nephrotoxicity.
adverse_effects: Cinchonism (tinnitus, temporary blindness, blurred vision, hot skin), hypoglycemia, nephrotoxicity.
dosage: Oral: Adult 300-600 mg q8h for 5-7 days; Child 25 mg/kg. IV Infusion (if unable to swallow): Loading 900 mg - 1.4 g over 4 hrs, then 300-600 mg q8h.
dosage_schedule: Oral: Adult 300-600 mg q8h for 5-7 days; Child 25 mg/kg. IV Infusion (if unable to swallow): Loading 900 mg - 1.4 g over 4 hrs, then 300-600 mg q8h.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose/electrolytes during IV use.
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, optic neuritis, digoxin toxicity, blood dyscrasia.
interactions: Additive vagolytic effect with anticholinergics. QT prolongation by macrolides/quinolones.

name: SULFADOXINE and PYRIMETHAMINE
uses: Combination therapy in P. falciparum malaria.
indications: Combination therapy in P. falciparum malaria.
side_effects: Hyperkalemia, rash, headache.
adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, rash, headache.
dosage: Treatment: adult 3 tablets single dose; child: 1.25 mg/kg pyrimethamine and 25 mg/kg sulphadoxine.
dosage_schedule: Treatment: adult 3 tablets single dose; child: 1.25 mg/kg pyrimethamine and 25 mg/kg sulphadoxine.
precautions: Predisposition to folate deficiency or hyperkalemia. Maintain fluid intake to avert crystalluria.
contraindications: Acute porphyrias, sulfonamide allergy, infants <6 weeks.
interactions: Folic acid decreases effects. Increases chlorpromazine levels.

name: ETHAMBUTOL
uses: Tuberculosis in combination.
indications: Tuberculosis in combination.
side_effects: Optic neuritis (reversible; dose-dependent), hyperuricemia, joint pain.
adverse_effects: Optic neuritis (reversible; dose-dependent), hyperuricemia, joint pain.
dosage: 15-25 mg/kg daily.
dosage_schedule: 15-25 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Check visual acuity (Snellen chart) and renal function before treatment. Monitor children ophthalmologically.
contraindications: Children <5 yrs, optic neuritis, severe renal impairment.
interactions: Decreases live BCG vaccine effects. Aluminium hydroxide increases levels.

name: ISONIAZID
uses: Tuberculosis in combination, TB prophylaxis.
indications: Tuberculosis in combination, TB prophylaxis.
side_effects: Peripheral neuritis (common), hepatic damage, skin rash.
adverse_effects: Peripheral neuritis (common), hepatic damage, skin rash.
dosage: 300 mg daily; Child: 10 mg/kg daily (max 300 mg).
dosage_schedule: 300 mg daily; Child: 10 mg/kg daily (max 300 mg).
precautions: Assessment of liver damage monthly. Administer Pyridoxine (25-100 mg daily) to prevent peripheral neuropathy. Caution in alcohol dependence (assess liver in first 2 months).
interactions: Increases toxicity with alcohol, cycloserine, rifampin, phenytoin. Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs. Aluminium antacids decrease absorption.

name: PYRAZINAMIDE
uses: Tuberculosis.
indications: Tuberculosis.
side_effects: Hepatotoxicity, hyperuricemia, sideroblastic anaemia, thrombocytopenia.
adverse_effects: Hepatotoxicity, hyperuricemia, sideroblastic anaemia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Adult (<50 kg): 1.5 g/day; (>50 kg): 2 g/day. Child: 25-35 mg/kg daily.
dosage_schedule: Adult (<50 kg): 1.5 g/day; (>50 kg): 2 g/day. Child: 25-35 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Assess RFT and LFT at onset. Monitor for gout.

name: RIFAMPIN
uses: Short course chemo for TB and leprosy, meningococcal prophylaxis, H. influenzae, atrophic rhinitis.
indications: Short course chemo for TB and leprosy, meningococcal prophylaxis, H. influenzae, atrophic rhinitis.
side_effects: Flu-like syndrome, thrombocytopenic purpura, transient rise in bilirubin.
adverse_effects: Flu-like syndrome, thrombocytopenic purpura, transient rise in bilirubin.
dosage: TB (>50 kg): 600 mg daily. Leprosy (Multibacillary): 600 mg once monthly supervised. Meningococcal Prophylaxis: 600 mg q12h for 2 days. Child (>1 yr): 10 mg/kg. Atrophic Rhinitis: 600 mg daily for 12 weeks.
dosage_schedule: TB (>50 kg): 600 mg daily. Leprosy (Multibacillary): 600 mg once monthly supervised. Meningococcal Prophylaxis: 600 mg q12h for 2 days. Child (>1 yr): 10 mg/kg. Atrophic Rhinitis: 600 mg daily for 12 weeks.
precautions: Induces hepatic enzymes. Urine, saliva, feces, sputum, sweat, and tears may be colored red-orange; soft contact lenses permanently stained. Avoid alcohol.
interactions: Accelerates metabolism of corticosteroids, digitalis, OCPs, oral hypoglycemics. Increases hepatotoxicity with isoniazid. Don't use with protease inhibitors.

name: STREPTOMYCIN
uses: TB resistant to other treatment, brucellosis, bacterial endocarditis.
indications: TB resistant to other treatment, brucellosis, bacterial endocarditis.
side_effects: Vestibular damage (increases with dose and age >40), nephrotoxicity, skin rashes.
adverse_effects: Vestibular damage (increases with dose and age >40), nephrotoxicity, skin rashes.
dosage: Adult: 0.75 g daily; child 15-20 mg/kg IM.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 0.75 g daily; child 15-20 mg/kg IM.
precautions: Avoid whenever possible in pregnancy/elderly. See under GENTAMICIN.

name: BEDAQUILINE
uses: Combination regimen for pulmonary MDR-TB when other treatments are not available.
indications: Combination regimen for pulmonary MDR-TB when other treatments are not available.
side_effects: Arthralgia, nausea, QT interval prolongation, myalgia.
adverse_effects: Arthralgia, nausea, QT interval prolongation, myalgia.
dosage: Adult: 400 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then 200 mg 3 times a week (at least 48 hrs between doses) for 22 weeks.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 400 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then 200 mg 3 times a week (at least 48 hrs between doses) for 22 weeks.
precautions: Monitor ECG baseline and at least monthly (QT prolongation risk). Caution in cardiac impairment, heart failure, syncope, thyroid disease.
interactions: Increases QT with class IA/III antiarrhythmics, haloperidol, chloroquine. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase effect (avoid >14 days). Lopinavir/ritonavir increase adverse reactions.

name: CAPREOMYCIN
uses: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
indications: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
side_effects: Induration at site, hearing loss with tinnitus/vertigo, leucocytosis, leucopenia, nephrotoxicity.
adverse_effects: Induration at site, hearing loss with tinnitus/vertigo, leucocytosis, leucopenia, nephrotoxicity.
dosage: Deep IM (Adult): 1 g daily (max 20 mg/kg) for 2-4 months, then 1 g 2-3 times a week.
dosage_schedule: Deep IM (Adult): 1 g daily (max 20 mg/kg) for 2-4 months, then 1 g 2-3 times a week.
precautions: Monitor renal, hepatic, auditory and vestibular function. Caution in breastfeeding/elderly.
interactions: Increased nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity with colistin, polymyxins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides.

name: CYCLOSERINE
uses: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
indications: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
side_effects: Confusion, convulsions, tremor, allergic dermatitis, megaloblastic anemia.
adverse_effects: Confusion, convulsions, tremor, allergic dermatitis, megaloblastic anemia.
dosage: Initially 250 mg q12h for 2 weeks, then 500 mg q12h. Child: 10 mg/kg/day divided.
dosage_schedule: Initially 250 mg q12h for 2 weeks, then 500 mg q12h. Child: 10 mg/kg/day divided.
precautions: Blood concentration monitoring required (should not exceed 30 mg/litre). Monitor hematological/renal function.
contraindications: Alcohol dependence, depression, epilepsy, psychotic states.
interactions: Alcohol increases convulsion risk. Isoniazid increases CNS toxicity.

name: ETHIONAMIDE
uses: Second line drug for TB.
indications: Second line drug for TB.
side_effects: Gynaecomastia, hypoglycemia, impotence, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis.
adverse_effects: Gynaecomastia, hypoglycemia, impotence, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis.
dosage: Initial 250 mg/day for 1-2 days, then 250 mg BID for 1-2 days, then gradual increase to highest tolerated. Avg 750 mg/day; max 1 g/day in divided doses.
dosage_schedule: Initial 250 mg/day for 1-2 days, then 250 mg BID for 1-2 days, then gradual increase to highest tolerated. Avg 750 mg/day; max 1 g/day in divided doses.
precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, psychiatric cases.
interactions: Increases toxicity with cycloserine. Increases isoniazid levels. Decreases magnesium oxide effect.

name: KANAMYCIN
uses: 2nd line drug in TB.
indications: 2nd line drug in TB.
side_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.
adverse_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.
dosage: IM: 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h. IV Infusion: 15-30 mg/kg q8-12h.
dosage_schedule: IM: 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h. IV Infusion: 15-30 mg/kg q8-12h.
precautions: See under GENTAMICIN.
contraindications: Pregnancy, renal impairment, myasthenia gravis, cochlear implant.

name: P-AMINOSALICYLIC ACID (PAS)
uses: 2nd line drugs in TB.
indications: 2nd line drugs in TB.
side_effects: Epigastric pain, goiter, blood dyscrasias.
adverse_effects: Epigastric pain, goiter, blood dyscrasias.
dosage: Granules: 4 g or 9.2 g sachet. Tablet: 500 mg.
dosage_schedule: Granules: 4 g or 9.2 g sachet. Tablet: 500 mg.
precautions: Take with meals to decrease epigastric pain.

name: ENTECAVIR
uses: Chronic hepatitis B (HBV).
indications: Chronic hepatitis B (HBV).
side_effects: Raised serum amylase/lipase, sleep disturbances, alopecia, thrombocytopenia.
adverse_effects: Raised serum amylase/lipase, sleep disturbances, alopecia, thrombocytopenia.
dosage: Compensated liver (Naive): 0.5 mg once daily. Lamivudine-resistant: 1 mg once daily. Decompensated liver: 1 mg once daily.
dosage_schedule: Compensated liver (Naive): 0.5 mg once daily. Lamivudine-resistant: 1 mg once daily. Decompensated liver: 1 mg once daily.
precautions: Reduce dose if eGFR <50 ml/min. Monitor liver function every 3 months. Recurrent hepatitis may occur on discontinuation.

name: PEGINTERFERON ALFA
uses: Combined with ribavirin for chronic Hep C, monotherapy for Hep C or Hep B.
indications: Combined with ribavirin for chronic Hep C, monotherapy for Hep C or Hep B.
side_effects: Anorexia, lethargy, arrhythmias, cardiovascular problems, myelosuppression, psoriasiform rash, seizures (elderly high dose).
adverse_effects: Anorexia, lethargy, arrhythmias, cardiovascular problems, myelosuppression, psoriasiform rash, seizures (elderly high dose).
dosage: Adult: SC 1.5 mcg/kg/week (max 150 mcg/week). Naive/Relapsed: 12 weeks. Non-responders: up to 24 weeks.
dosage_schedule: Adult: SC 1.5 mcg/kg/week (max 150 mcg/week). Naive/Relapsed: 12 weeks. Non-responders: up to 24 weeks.
precautions: Monitor lipid concentration. Monitoring closely in mild-moderate hepatic impairment. Renal impairment: reduce dose.

name: SOFOSBUVIR
uses: Chronic hepatitis C.
indications: Chronic hepatitis C.
side_effects: Hyperbilirubinemia, headache, fatigue, anaemia.
adverse_effects: Hyperbilirubinemia, headache, fatigue, anaemia.
dosage: Oral: 400 mg once daily.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 400 mg once daily.
precautions: Use two forms of reliable contraceptives. Avoid breastfeeding.
interactions: Decreased by P-glycoprotein inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin). Bradycardia with amiodarone. Increased by carvedilol.

name: ACYCLOVIR
uses: Herpes infections, mucocutaneous HSV, infectious mononucleosis, Varicella, Herpes zoster; Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis and herpes zoster ophthalmicus associated keratitis; Cold sores (Herpes Simplex); oral lesions related to chicken pox and shingles
indications: Herpes infections, mucocutaneous HSV, infectious mononucleosis, Varicella, Herpes zoster; Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis and herpes zoster ophthalmicus associated keratitis; Cold sores (Herpes Simplex); oral lesions related to chicken pox and shingles
side_effects: Rashes, urticaria, increase in blood urea/creatinine, fatigue; Local burning and stinging, blepharitis, superficial punctate keratitis; Stinging and burning sensation after application; mouth pain (buccal tablet)
adverse_effects: Rashes, urticaria, increase in blood urea/creatinine, fatigue; Local burning and stinging, blepharitis, superficial punctate keratitis; Stinging and burning sensation after application; mouth pain (buccal tablet)
dosage: HSV Treatment: 200 mg 5 times daily (5 days); Recurrence prevention: 200 mg QID or 400 mg BID; Varicella/Zoster (Adult): 800 mg 5 times daily (7 days); (Child): 20 mg/kg; Mucocutaneous: 400 mg 5 times daily; Topical: apply every 4 hrs; Ointment: apply 5 times a day for 2 weeks to 3 weeks; 200 mg 5 times daily for 10 days; Recurrent prophylaxis: 400 mg twice daily for 10 days
dosage_schedule: HSV Treatment: 200 mg 5 times daily (5 days); Recurrence prevention: 200 mg QID or 400 mg BID; Varicella/Zoster (Adult): 800 mg 5 times daily (7 days); (Child): 20 mg/kg; Mucocutaneous: 400 mg 5 times daily; Topical: apply every 4 hrs; Ointment: apply 5 times a day for 2 weeks to 3 weeks; 200 mg 5 times daily for 10 days; Recurrent prophylaxis: 400 mg twice daily for 10 days
precautions: Caution in renal impairment; Do not give concurrently with live vaccines; Immunization should be up to date before treatment; Should be administered within the first 72 hours of symptom onset
interactions: Increases serious infections when used with TNF-alpha blockers

name: OSELTAMIVIR
uses: Prevention and treatment of influenza A or B.
indications: Prevention and treatment of influenza A or B.
side_effects: Seizures, toxic epidermolysis necrolysis, SJS.
adverse_effects: Seizures, toxic epidermolysis necrolysis, SJS.
dosage: Influenza: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Prevention: 75 mg once daily for 10 days. Post-exposure Prophylaxis: up to 6 weeks.
dosage_schedule: Influenza: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Prevention: 75 mg once daily for 10 days. Post-exposure Prophylaxis: up to 6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid use with H1N1 virus vaccine or intranasal influenza vaccine.

name: DIDANOSINE
uses: HIV infection.
indications: HIV infection.
side_effects: Acute renal failure, optic nerve changes, parotid gland enlargement, gynaecomastia.
adverse_effects: Acute renal failure, optic nerve changes, parotid gland enlargement, gynaecomastia.
dosage: Oral Adult (60 kg): 250 mg daily (1-2 divided doses); (>60 kg): 400 mg daily. Take 2 hours before or after food.
dosage_schedule: Oral Adult (60 kg): 250 mg daily (1-2 divided doses); (>60 kg): 400 mg daily. Take 2 hours before or after food.
precautions: Monitor annually: visual acuity, color vision, dilated fundus. Risk of peripheral neuropathy (dose-related). Sodium restricted diets caution. Monitor amylase.
interactions: Increased by allopurinol, tenofovir. Pancreatitis risk increased by stavudine. Decreased absorption by antacids, ketoconazole, dapsone, quinolones.

name: EFAVIRENZ
uses: HIV infections.
indications: HIV infections.
side_effects: Rash, SJS, depression, ataxia, cognitive impairment.
adverse_effects: Rash, SJS, depression, ataxia, cognitive impairment.
dosage: 600 mg once daily (Adult/Child >40 kg).
dosage_schedule: 600 mg once daily (Adult/Child >40 kg).
precautions: Moderate-severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function if co-administering hepatotoxic drugs. If dose missed, take as remembered; do not double.
interactions: Increased CNS depression with alcohol, antidepressants. Increases ritonavir/estrogens. Increases warfarin/statins. Decreases OCPs, ketoconazole.

name: INDINAVIR
uses: See under SAQUINAVIR.
indications: See under SAQUINAVIR.
side_effects: Hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, paraesthesia.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, paraesthesia.
dosage: 800 mg q8h. Child: 500 mg/m2 q8h (max 800 mg q8h).
dosage_schedule: 800 mg q8h. Child: 500 mg/m2 q8h (max 800 mg q8h).
precautions: Ensure adequate hydration (risk of nephrolithiasis). Caution in diabetes, hemophilia, chronic Hep B/C.
interactions: Dysrhythmias with ergots, amiodarone. Increases statins (myopathy risk). Increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors. Decreased by CYP3A4 inducers (St. John's wort, rifamycins).

name: LAMIVUDINE
uses: HIV infection in combination.
indications: HIV infection in combination.
side_effects: Alopecia, anaemia, peripheral neuropathy.
adverse_effects: Alopecia, anaemia, peripheral neuropathy.
dosage: Adult: 150 mg BID or 300 mg daily. Infant (<1 mo): 2 mg/kg BID. Child (1 mo+): 4 mg/kg BID (max 300 mg).
dosage_schedule: Adult: 150 mg BID or 300 mg daily. Infant (<1 mo): 2 mg/kg BID. Child (1 mo+): 4 mg/kg BID (max 300 mg).
precautions: Renal disease, pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy. Caution in Hep B/C co-infection.
interactions: Increased by cotrimoxazole, amiloride, entecavir, metformin. Interferons decrease its effects.

name: LOPINAVIR + RITONAVIR
uses: HIV infection.
indications: HIV infection.
